messages:
maya (oncall): paging in — multiple decode/stream nodes spiking CUDA OOMs, requests dropping with 502/connection reset. seeing huge token counts on a subset of sessions. customers reporting truncated responses.
incident-bot: Incident created: RID-2026-03-15-01 · Severity: P2 · Alert: gpu-decode-oom-surge · Pager: maya (oncall) · Runbook: /runbooks/decode-oom.md
ben (infra): grabbing logs now. are we seeing a config change or traffic pattern? any recent rollout?
carla (eng-runtime): not seeing recent runtime deploys in last hour. preliminary traces show many streams with max_tokens unset (null) or very large values from a single client key. looks like prefix runaway generation.
dave (sre): memory profiles attached to the alert show steady KV growth, then sudden spikes followed by cudaError: out of memory. likely unbounded attention growth due to unbounded max_tokens / stop tokens missing.
maya (oncall): impact: 14% request drop rate to /v1/streams/generate for region us-west-2 in the last 7m. top affected customers: cust-A (chatbot), cust-F (document-summarize). notifying support.
sam (support): pinging customers now, will collect request ids.
ellie (cust-succ): flagged high-touch customers, sending notice "we're investigating; temporary throttles applied".
carla (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: 1) global per-api-key max_tokens cap via edge header enforcement (patching gateway) 2) route heavy keys to quantized model variant (q8_16) 3) enable streaming token backpressure (throttle by tokens/second). pushing config changes now.
ben (infra): scaling decode pool +2 nodes while we apply mitigations (doing rolling scale to avoid eviction storms).
maya (oncall): command to set gateway cap (example):
```
PATCH /internal/gateway/config
{
  "stream_max_tokens": 1024,
  "max_tokens_mode": "enforce"
}
```
apply now?
carla (eng-runtime): apply. also toggling automatic prefix eviction to aggressive for the next 10m to reclaim KV memory: `eviction.window=10m aggressive=true`
dave (sre): watchlist: cuda-oom, container_restarts, grpc-502, kv-cache-size. alert thresholds lowered.
incident-bot: Change deployed by carla — gateway cap=1024 enforced.
ben (infra): scale up complete +2 decode nodes, transient CPU pressure on scheduler but no node flaps.
maya (oncall): after cap enforcement: request drops down to 2.8% (was 14%). stream latency slight bump for long sessions but overall throughput stabilized.
carla (eng-runtime): routing heavy keys now to q8_16 variant, verifying token-quality regression tests. early checks OK.
dave (sre): noticed one container crashed during eviction window, auto-restarted. collecting core dump.
carla (eng-runtime): core dump shows large attention KV allocation growth leading up to OOM — confirms runaway generation. root cause likely client not setting max_tokens or we misrouted a legacy SDK that omits client-side caps.
maya (oncall): next actions: 1) keep gateway cap for 2h 2) keep eviction aggressive for 30m 3) postmortem + contact engineering to audit client-side SDKs and gateway default headers 4) support to message customers with ETA. tagging product for opt-in safety defaults.
ellie (cust-succ): sending targeted message to cust-A and cust-F now, offering logs and mitigation summary.
sam (support): collecting request-ids for cust-A: rids: [r_abc123, r_def456] — uploaded to support bucket.
ben (infra): putting an automated guard in the autoscaler to avoid ramping too fast and causing eviction cascades; new threshold rule applied.
carla (eng-runtime): follow-up hotfix: 1) default SDK header injection `x-client-max-tokens=512` for older SDKs without explicit max_tokens 2) additional runtime check to reject streams with no stopping signals and extremely high token budgets (>5000). will PR and fast-track.
maya (oncall): handoff to ben for monitoring; ben will be on until 03:00 UTC. carla will own the postmortem + fix.
ben (infra): monitoring looks stable. request drop baseline returned to <1% after 20m. leaving temporary caps in place.
dave (sre): recording incident notes and timeline. recommend customer credits due to partial service degradation.
carla (eng-runtime): PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2628 (hotfix + SDK header injection). please review.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=stabilized · severity downgraded to P3 · duration=43m · responder=maya,ben,carla,dave
maya (oncall): thanks team. final: we'll run a focused postmortem, deploy SDK header backfill, and roll out a rule to surface keys with repeated high token usage. handing off to ben as oncall.
ben (infra): taking over. if anything flares, ping me @ben. :thumbsup:
